target: Kami akan berkumpul di rumah nenek hari Minggu.
english: We will gather at grandma's house on Sunday.
tip: minggu means week, but Minggu with a capital M is Sunday: hari Minggu = on Sunday, minggu depan = next week. Case decides.

target: Bagaimana kalau kita bertemu jam sepuluh saja?
english: How about we meet at ten instead?
tip: saja softens suggestions: jam sepuluh saja = let's just make it ten.

target: Dia selalu sibuk, susah sekali ditelepon.
english: He is always busy, very hard to reach by phone.
tip: susah + a di- verb = 'hard to get X-ed': susah ditelepon = hard to reach, literally 'hard to be phoned'. Same pattern with other verbs: susah dicari = hard to find.

target: HP saya mati, jadi saya pinjam HP teman.
english: My phone died, so I borrowed a friend's phone.
tip: HP (say: ha-pe) is the spoken word for phone: HP saya mati = my phone died.

target: Kamar mandi ada di lantai dua.
english: The bathroom is on the second floor.
tip: lantai dua = the second floor: storeys use plain numbers after lantai.

target: Mobil merah itu punya tetangga kami.
english: That red car belongs to our neighbor.
tip: Adjectives follow the noun: mobil merah = red car (lit. car red).

target: Kulkas kami rusak sejak kemarin sore.
english: Our fridge has been broken since yesterday afternoon.
tip: English needs 'has been broken since' – Indonesian just states the fact: rusak sejak kemarin sore = broken since yesterday afternoon. No perfect tense exists.

target: Lampu di kamar mandi tidak mau menyala.
english: The light in the bathroom will not turn on.
tip: tidak mau + verb for things = won't: lampunya tidak mau menyala = it won't turn on.

target: Tolong nyalakan lampu ruang tamu, sudah gelap.
english: Please turn on the living room light, it is dark already.
tip: -kan turns a state into an action: menyala = be on, nyalakan = turn it on.

target: Jangan lupa mematikan kompor sebelum pergi.
english: Do not forget to turn off the stove before leaving.
tip: mematikan = to turn off (lit. make dead): mematikan lampu = turn off the light.

target: Kaus kaki saya hilang sebelah di kamar.
english: One of my socks is missing in the room.
tip: sebelah = one of a pair: hilang sebelah = one of the two is missing.

target: Kami makan malam di meja kayu yang besar.
english: We have dinner at the big wooden table.
tip: yang picks out 'the ... one': meja yang besar = the big table.

target: Karpet ruang tamu kami merah tua.
english: Our living room carpet is dark red.
tip: tua darkens a color, muda lightens it: merah tua = dark red; biru muda = light blue.

target: Tas hijau di kursi itu punya siapa?
english: Whose green bag is that on the chair?
tip: punya siapa? = whose?: Tas ini punya siapa? = whose bag is this?

target: Jaket hitam itu tergantung di belakang pintu.
english: That black jacket is hanging behind the door.
tip: ter- describes a state: tergantung = hanging; tertutup = closed.

target: Saya cari hotel yang dekat dengan stasiun.
english: I am looking for a hotel that is near the station.
tip: yang links a noun to its description: hotel yang dekat = a hotel that is near.

target: Kereta lebih cepat daripada bus ke bandara.
english: The train is faster than the bus to the airport.
tip: lebih ... daripada = more ... than: lebih cepat daripada bus = faster than the bus.

target: Boleh saya lihat kamarnya dulu?
english: May I see the room first?
tip: Boleh saya lihat kamarnya? asks permission – and boleh alone is also the answer: Boleh! = sure, go ahead. One word for both the asking and the granting.

target: Bisa minta peta kota ini?
english: Can I get a map of this city?
tip: Bisa minta peta? is the complete everyday request – no subject, no 'give me' verb. minta = ask for a thing; bisa softens it into 'can I get...?'

target: Tadi saya sudah beli tiket kereta di loket.
english: Earlier I already bought train tickets at the counter.
tip: tadi = earlier today: tadi saya sudah beli = I already bought (it) earlier.

target: Jangan lupa bawa paspor dan tiket kamu.
english: Don't forget to bring your passport and ticket.
tip: jangan lupa = don't forget, the go-to reminder opener: jangan lupa bawa paspor. jangan negates commands; tidak lupa would just describe someone who doesn't forget.

target: Tolong antar koper ini ke kamar saya.
english: Please take this suitcase to my room.
tip: tolong + verb = please (do something): tolong antar = please take (it) there.

target: Kemarin kami menginap di hotel dekat bandara.
english: Yesterday we stayed overnight at a hotel near the airport.
tip: The me- prefix turns a root into an active verb: inap (stay over) becomes menginap = to stay overnight. Kami menginap di hotel = we stayed at a hotel.

target: Kalau kamu capek, kita istirahat di kafe itu.
english: If you are tired, we can rest at that cafe.
tip: kita includes the person you're talking to, kami leaves them out – kita istirahat works because the listener is invited to rest too.

target: Laporan yang kamu kirim kemarin sudah saya baca.
english: I have already read the report you sent yesterday.
tip: yang also points back to things: laporan yang kamu kirim = the report you sent.

target: Boleh saya pulang lebih awal hari ini?
english: May I go home earlier today?
tip: English can does double duty; Indonesian splits it: boleh = allowed to, bisa = able to. Boleh saya pulang? asks permission, not ability.

target: Kirim laporan itu paling lambat hari Jumat.
english: Send that report by Friday at the latest.
tip: paling lambat is literally 'slowest' – Indonesian deadlines are superlatives: paling lambat hari Jumat = by Friday at the latest.

target: Tolong jelaskan bagian ini sekali lagi.
english: Please explain this part one more time.
tip: -kan turns a word into a doing-verb: jelas (clear) → jelaskan = explain.

target: Besok kami akan rapat dengan tim pemasaran.
english: Tomorrow we will have a meeting with the marketing team.
tip: akan marks the future, but a time word can carry it alone: with besok in the sentence, kami akan rapat could drop the akan. It just makes 'will' explicit.

target: Kalau rapat batal, saya langsung kabari kamu.
english: If the meeting is cancelled, I'll let you know right away.
tip: -i makes a verb aim at someone: kabar (news) → kabari = let (someone) know.
